title: HOSA Nutrition: Medical Nutrition Therapy - Nutrition - Medical Nutrition Therapy - Oncology
subject: Nutrition

questions.q: A chemotherapy patient is experiencing severe neutropenia (low white blood cell count). Which food safety practice is critical for this patient?
options: Eating fresh, organic salads from a buffet.
Consuming raw sushi to increase protein intake.
Avoiding raw fruits/vegetables unless peeled/cooked and ensuring meat is well-done.
questions.explain: Neutropenic patients are highly susceptible to infection. A low-microbial (neutropenic) diet often excludes raw unpeeled produce, raw meats/fish, and unpasteurized items to minimize pathogen exposure.
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: A cancer patient reports 'dysgeusia' (altered taste), specifically stating that meat tastes metallic. Which intervention is most helpful?
options: Force them to eat red meat.
Use plastic utensils instead of metal ones and marinate meats.
questions.explain: Using plastic utensils reduces the metallic sensation. Marinades and cold/room-temp foods can also improve palatability.
